title: Star trails over Atacama Desert Cacti
caption: Star trails over cacti in the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Star trails circle the South Celestial Pole above a still landscape dotted with cacti in Chile's Atacama Desert. The trails record the stars' apparent paths as Earth slowly turns, built up through long exposures.

Over the trails, a final, deeper exposure was laid on top. It brings out a host of fainter stars and, low on the horizon, the rising southern Milky Way, mottled with dark dust and marked by the familiar pink glow of the Carina Nebula.

Toward the right are the Milky Way's satellite galaxies, the Large Magellanic Cloud near the top centre and the Small Magellanic Cloud at the bottom right. Combining trails with one deep frame lets the picture show both the motion of the sky and faint detail that the trails alone would smear out.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based composite by B. Tafreshi of long exposures for the star trails, with a final deeper exposure superimposed. The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees neither the trails nor so many faint stars. Both come from the camera recording light over long exposures.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

alt: Circular star trails over a desert landscape with cacti, with the Milky Way and a pink glow rising at the horizon and two fuzzy patches toward the right.
